reason: The text passage from Nehemiah 4 demonstrates Yahweh actively helping the Hebrew people (Judah) rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. Key evidence includes: (1) The people's prayer 'Hear, O our God; for we are despised' calling for divine intervention; (2) God's direct action: 'And God frustrated their counsel' (וַיָּפֶר הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת־עֲצָתָם), which thwarted the enemies' plans; (3) The assurance 'our God will fight for us' (אֱלֹהֵינוּ יִלָּחֶם לָנוּ), positioning God as their defender; and (4) The successful completion of the wall-building project. The narrative structure shows Yahweh responding to the people's need and actively opposing their enemies' attempts to prevent the construction, indicating that assisting the Hebrew people's objectives aligns with Yahweh's purposes.
